result.title: Structured Priors: Towards an algebra of component priors for prior-data fitted networks
result.summary: Prior-data fitted networks are typically trained using synthetic data generated by a single, manually constructed generator. In cases where such a generator combines multiple components, e.g., in TabPFN, Mitra, or TabICLv2, this is achieved through a mixture using manually specified weights, the impact of which on the network only becomes apparent after pre-training. Instead of such a hand-built generator, this work proposes a structured prior: a small set of named component priors, linked by operators whose algebraic properties are formally proven and whose influence on the trained network has been validated. Within a measure-theoretic framework, the operators of mixture, convolution, amplitude scaling, local transform, and projection are defined. Their governing laws are proven. These operators are implemented in the macl2l software package. Experiments demonstrate that the implemented generators reproduce the identities within the resolution of a permutation test. Furthermore, it is shown that trained networks obey the distributive law; that a mixed prior composed of small components performs as well as or better than any individual component in seven out of eight open regression benchmarks; and that on two of these tables a structured prior reaches, with a ninth of the data budget, an error that a generic random-function prior does not reach even with the full budget. A theorem on model averaging demonstrates that networks trained on individual components constitute the Bayes predictor for the mixture, provided that the component networks are themselves the Bayes predictors for their respective priors. However, the pre-registered test of this averaged predictor with trained component networks failed, because the networks identify the generating component too rarely. The paper proposes a research program focused on the algebra of structured priors for prior-data fitted networks.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作为 prior-data fitted networks 提出「结构化先验」：用混合、卷积、幅度缩放、局部变换与投影等算子，将少量具名分量先验组合成合成数据生成器，并证明其代数性质、给出 macl2l 实现与回归基准验证，同时检验分量网络平均是否构成混合先验的 Bayes 预测器。
AI.relevance_reason: 其分量先验的可组合代数与模型平均定理，可能为 LVR 训练任务分布的配比设计及「多路训练信号如何汇入同一推理行为」提供形式化参照，但与原论文的视觉状态或证据使用无直接关联，需核查可迁移性。
